perf.summary: Marshal.AllocHGlobal does not honor the requested alignment, and the alignInBytes parameter is silently ignored across all overloads.
perf.currentCost: AllocHGlobal returns memory aligned only to the platform malloc granularity (typically 16 bytes on 64-bit). Callers expecting larger alignInBytes (e.g. 32/64 for SIMD/cacheline) get misaligned pointers, forcing scalar or split loads in downstream Burst-vectorized code (a real per-iteration cycle cost in hot loops that consume these buffers).
perf.proposedChange: For the alignment-bearing overloads, over-allocate sizeInBytes + alignInBytes, align the returned pointer up via (p + (align-1)) & ~(nint)(align-1), and store the original base pointer in the bytes immediately preceding the aligned pointer so Free can recover it; or document that alignment is not honored. Since alignInBytes is a power of two by Unity convention, the round-up is a single add+and (branchless).
perf.rationale: Correct alignment lets downstream code use aligned vector loads/stores instead of unaligned or split accesses, and avoids cacheline-straddling reads. The align math itself is branchless add+and.
perf.risk: Changes the free path (must subtract the stored offset), so it is NOT a drop-in for the current Free which calls FreeHGlobal directly on the same pointer. This is a correctness-coupled change: only safe if Free is updated in lockstep. If callers never request alignment > malloc granularity, this is a no-op and can be skipped. Power-of-two alignment assumed (true for Unity allocators).

perf.summary: Marshal.AllocHGlobal / FreeHGlobal are managed P/Invoke calls that Burst cannot compile; on the hot path inside Burst-compiled jobs these allocators are not Burst-compatible.
perf.currentCost: Any Burst-compiled method that calls these allocators will fail to compile or fall back to managed (Mono) execution, losing all Burst vectorization/codegen for the calling job. This defeats the stated 'runs under Unity Burst' goal for allocation-bearing paths.
perf.proposedChange: For Burst compatibility use UnsafeUtility.Malloc/Free (or a raw malloc/free via a Burst-callable function pointer) instead of Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal. If this module is intentionally the non-Burst fallback shim, annotate it so callers know allocation must happen outside Burst regions.
perf.rationale: UnsafeUtility.Malloc is Burst-intrinsified and also takes alignment directly, simultaneously fixing the alignment gap above. Removes the managed transition entirely.
perf.risk: This is the NoDeps module that deliberately avoids UnityEngine/Unity.Collections internals, so UnsafeUtility may be unavailable by design. If so, reject; this is a structural/dependency tradeoff, not a free micro-opt. Behavior of allocation size is identical; only the backing allocator changes.
